title.narrative: Envelope 3: Contingency Plan for Rapid response for Displacement and Return

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtBO proposes a 12-month multi-sectoral emergency intervention in Idleb and Aleppo governorates to address sudden displacement caused by conflict escalation, natural hazards (floods, snowstorms, drought), or returns following insecurity elsewhere. The intervention combines MPCA, Emergency SNFIs, Health, and Protection (including GBV and CP) components to deliver integrated life-saving support within 48–72 hours of crisis onset.ltbrgtTargeting newly displaced populations, returnees, and host communities, especially women, children, PwDs, and elderly persons, the project includes rapid deployment of mobile protection teams, provision of cash and winter NFIs, emergency shelter kits, health kits and medicines, and community-based PSS and safe spaces. This approach leverages BO’s operational presence, local networks, and track record of successful rapid responses in NWS, ensuring coverage of remote and high-severity areas with agility and accountability.ltbrgt-MPCA: BaO will deliver cash assistance to highly vulnerable HHs. This modality ensures flexible, dignified, and efficient support that allows affected families to prioritize their own urgent needs, whether food, shelter, medicines, or transport. The response adheres to the 2025 MPC Sector Strategy and contributes to HRP SO1 by enabling crisis-affected populations to cope with the initial shock of displacement.ltbrgt-Protection: The protection response directly contributes to Protection SO1, 3, and 4, while addressing the urgent safety and dignity risks in newly established shelters. Mobile protection teams will deploy within 48–72 hours to conduct protection risk assessments, offer psychological first aid (PFA), and facilitate safe referrals to essential services. Community-based protection desks and safe spaces will be established to offer confidential support and guidance, particularly for women and children.ltbrgtThe intervention includes GBV risk mitigation through the distribution of dignity kits, training of staff and community focal points on GBV and PSEA, and engagement with the GBV AoR to ensure that survivors are referred safely to specialized services. Tailored child protection interventions will target vulnerable children with PSS, safe spaces, and structured awareness sessions to prevent exploitation, abuse, and neglect. The project also promotes community participation, strengthens protection feedback mechanisms, and integrates an age, gender, and disability-sensitive approach throughout.ltbrgt-Health: BO will support public health facilities and frontline service delivery with the provision of essential medicines, medical consumables, and emergency supplies in areas with high severity. The health intervention contributes directly to Health Cluster SO1, focusing on inclusive and equitable access to life-saving services for both displaced and host communities in Aleppo and Idleb. Special emphasis will be placed on maternal health, trauma response, management of chronic conditions, and care for PwDs and GBV survivors needing urgent medical support.ltbrgtThis component complements and builds upon BO’s previous health interventions in NWS. It also contributes to improving supply chain continuity, restoring the functionality of disrupted health facilities, and enhancing coordination with the WASH and Protection sectors for integrated service delivery.ltbrgt4- SNFI: To ensure dignity and immediate relief for newly displaced HHs, BO will distribute emergency NFI kits and basic shelter materials in collective centers and informal settlements. The kits follow SNFI Cluster-approved standards and are tailored to local needs. The intervention directly contributes to SNFI Cluster SO1 by ensuring immediate access to essential NFIs and shelter support for vulnerable groups, including female-headed HHs, PwDs, elderly persons, and those at risk of exclusion.ltbrgtThe response will coordinate with coordination bodies/channels, implementing partners, and local authorities to avoid duplication and ensure comprehensive coverage.lt/pgtltdivgtltdivgtlt/divgtlt/divgt
